claims.claim: Current provider receipt applies to current source and verifier bytes
claims.evidence: FILE_MANIFEST rows, START/RESULT identity inputs, recomputed execution identity; all matched

claims.claim: The finite numerical temperature contract avoids positivity, underflow, and cancellation failure in the implemented moments
claims.evidence: Static expn(2,x) positive representation; x spans about 0.789 to 78.911; saved normal positive moments and direct 80-digit quadrature maximum relative discrepancy 2.1974065901747693e-14 at three temperatures
claims.limit: Three-temperature numeric evidence is not a uniform error proof across all temperatures or physical calibration

claims.claim: transfer_u overflows at q=1 for the tested largest finite binary64 inputs
claims.evidence: TRANSFER_ENDPOINT_OBSERVATIONS.json: four calls returned finite exact endpoints including max binary64

claims.claim: Every boolean input element is rejected by _real
claims.evidence: _real starts with np.asarray(values), so a mixed sequence such as [True,0.5] becomes a float array before dtype checking
claims.limit: Pure boolean inputs and boolean-typed arrays are rejected; this is a narrow guard-description/API issue and does not invalidate existing numerical evidence

findings.evidence: dtype checking occurs after np.asarray coercion; mixed bool/numeric containers lose boolean identity
findings.impact: The docstring promise to reject bool is stronger than the actual element-level input guard. Example transfer_u(20.0,[True,0.5]) is accepted by static NumPy coercion reasoning. No demonstrated impact on the saved physical calculations.
findings.minimal_correction: Either document rejection as boolean-typed arrays only or validate mixed input elements before NumPy coercion; add only one affected guard case if strict element rejection is required.

overall: No blocking numerical defect established in the admitted scalar-moment implementation or its saved evidence. One low-severity input-guard wording/behavior mismatch. No claims about the separately authored net bridge.
